data.name: Finland
data.summary: Capital gains taxed at 34% at the top, listed dividends at an effective 28.9%. Inheritance tax per child: tax-free under EUR 30,000 (2026), then 7%-19%, about 18-19% on a large share. No wealth tax. EU member, no special regime for wealthy arrivals. A family investment Oy pays 20% on gains and dividends, and pays out lightly taxed unlisted-company dividends (7.5% on the first EUR 150,000 per shareholder within an 8% return).

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Capital income (gains, dividends, interest, rents) is taxed separately from earned income at 30%/34%.
regimes.eligibility: Permanent home or habitual abode in Finland, or continuous stay of more than 6 months.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are capital income taxed at 30% up to EUR 30,000 of total taxable capital income and 34% above. A large gain is therefore taxed at 34% at the margin, on listed or unlisted shares, domestic or foreign, and on real estate other than a qualifying main home.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Total sale prices of EUR 1,000 or less in a year are exempt. A home used as the owner's or family's permanent home for at least 2 years is exempt. Losses offset capital gains and then other capital income and carry forward 5 years. Equity savings account (osakesäästötili): gains and dividends inside the account are taxed only on withdrawal; contributions are capped (cap not verified in this research).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: No general exit tax for individuals. Finnish nationals remain resident for 3 calendar years after leaving unless they show no essential ties (see residency). Earn-out (conditional additional purchase price) gains are taxed in the year the amount is confirmed (2026 change).
open_questions: Equity savings account contribution cap for 2026 not confirmed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Top marginal capital income rate 34% (capital income above EUR 30,000 a year). No holding-period relief on the rate. The deemed acquisition cost (20% of the sale price, 40% if held at least 10 years) can lower the taxable gain when the real cost basis is low: with the 40% deemed cost the effective rate on proceeds is at most 0.6 x 34% = 20.4%. The JSON gives the statutory marginal rate on the gain.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities trading on a business scale can be treated as business income taxed partly as earned income at progressive rates (top marginal earned income rate about 52% in 2026). Ordinary portfolio management of a private investor is capital income.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for the rate. Holding period only changes the deemed acquisition cost (20% below 10 years, 40% from 10 years). FIFO per securities account.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains; foreign tax on the gain (usually none for portfolio shares) is creditable.

dividends.summary: Dividends from listed companies (Finnish, EU/EEA, or from countries with a tax treaty covering dividends, e.g. the US) are 85% taxable as capital income at 30%/34%, an effective top rate of 28.9%. Foreign withholding tax is credited up to the treaty rate.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: 15% of listed dividends exempt. Unlisted dividends within 8% of net asset value per share and EUR 150,000: 75% exempt.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign dividends from a non-EU/EEA country without a tax treaty covering dividends are fully taxable as earned income at progressive rates (top about 52%). Credit for foreign withholding is limited to the treaty maximum (Vero publishes the creditable maximum per treaty).

open_questions: Exact 2026 rules on the 35% WHT rate for nominee-registered shares not checked against Vero.
dividends.rate_basis: 85% of a listed-company dividend is taxable capital income; 0.85 x 34% = 28.9% at the top. Unlisted-company dividends: 25% taxable (7.5%/8.5% effective) on the part equal to an 8% return on the share's mathematical value up to EUR 150,000, 85% taxable above that within the 8% return, and 75% taxable as earned income beyond the 8% return.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Finnish companies withhold 30% (35% in some cases, e.g. nominee-registered shares where the owner is not identified) on dividends to non-resident individuals and 20% to non-resident companies, reduced by treaty; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% holding). Government proposal HE 151/2026 would cut the corporate WHT rate to 18% from 2027.
dividends.treaty_network: Broad network: PwC's dividend table lists about 76 treaty partners, including the US (15% portfolio WHT). The Finland-Russia treaty is suspended from 1 July 2026; no treaty in force with Portugal.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the 'holding_oy' structure regime: an unlisted Finnish Oy holding listed shares below 10% pays 20% on those dividends (100% taxable) and on gains; its own dividends to individuals are 25% taxable (7.5% effective) up to EUR 150,000 per shareholder within an 8% return on net assets.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax 0.41%-2.00% of taxable value (buildings 1.30%-2.00% general range). Transfer tax 3% on Finnish real property, 1.5% on shares of real estate companies and other Finnish securities; listed securities traded on a market are generally exempt.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax per heir. For children (tax class I), from 1 January 2026 inheritances under EUR 30,000 are tax-free; above that the whole share is taxed at progressive rates from 7% to 19% (19% on the part above EUR 1,000,000). A EUR 10 million share costs about EUR 1.86 million (18.6%).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Cliff: no tax under EUR 30,000; at EUR 30,000 the tax is EUR 100 plus 7% of the excess, EUR 149,000 at EUR 1,000,000 plus 19% of the excess. The brackets above omit the flat EUR 100 (immaterial for a large estate). Ordinary household goods exempt up to EUR 7,500. Spouse has additional deductions (not relevant to children).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Gifts received from the deceased within 3 years before death are added to the inheritance (gift tax already paid is credited). 2026 change: threshold raised from EUR 20,000 to EUR 30,000 and base amounts lowered; class I marginal rates unchanged.

open_questions: Additional deduction for minor children inheriting from a parent (historically EUR 60,000) not verified for 2026.
Whether the 3-year residence tail for Finnish nationals also applies to inheritance and gift tax was not verified.
inheritance.spouse_note: The spouse (and registered partner) is in tax class I and pays the same 7%-19% scale as children, with an extra EUR 90,000 spouse deduction from the taxable share (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act 12 §); on a EUR 10 million-plus share the effective rate is about 18.6%. Cohabitants without registration are not spouses.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gift tax for children: gifts from the same donor are aggregated over 3 years; total under EUR 7,500 is exempt (EUR 5,000 before 2026). Rates 8% to 17%: EUR 100 at 7,500 + 8%; EUR 1,400 at 25,000 + 10%; EUR 4,500 at 55,000 + 12%; EUR 21,900 at 200,000 + 15%; EUR 141,900 at 1,000,000 + 17% above. Gift tax is due when the donor or the recipient is Finnish-resident.
inheritance.business_relief: Generational transfer relief for a business or substantial company stake (inheritance and gift tax deferral/reduced valuation) exists; conditions not researched here. It does not cover a portfolio of listed shares.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide scope when the deceased or the heir was resident in Finland at the time of death; Finnish real estate and shares in Finnish real-estate-rich companies are always taxable. Foreign inheritance tax on the same assets is creditable.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Residence-based: if the deceased or the heir lives in Finland. Finnish nationals remain resident for income tax for 3 years after emigrating unless they show no essential ties; the equivalent effect for inheritance tax was not verified.

regimes.name: Private investment company (osakeyhtiö, Oy)
regimes.description: The family holds its portfolio through a Finnish private limited company (Oy). The company pays the 20% corporate rate on portfolio gains and on listed-share dividends (portfolio dividends are fully taxable in an unlisted company), instead of 34% / 28.9% personally. Withdrawals are dividends from an unlisted company, which are taxed lightly: within an 8% return on the shares' net asset value, 25% of the first EUR 150,000 per shareholder a year is taxable capital income (7.5% effective). No wealth tax; inheritance tax applies to the Oy shares as to other assets (inherited from the standard regime).
regimes.eligibility: Any Finnish resident can form an Oy (no minimum share capital for a private company). The low payout rate needs dividends within 8% of the mathematical (net asset) value of the shares and is per shareholder, so it scales with the number of adult family shareholders. US citizens are excluded: US CFC/PFIC rules tax the company's passive income currently.
regimes.duration_note: Ordinary company and dividend-tax rules with no time limit. The unlisted-dividend relief is under political review (a VATT/Etla study proposes changing it), but no change was enacted as of 2026-10-15.

structure.entity: Private limited company (osakeyhtiö, Oy) used as a family investment company
structure.payout_notes: Dividends from an unlisted company to a resident individual: up to an 8% return on the shares' mathematical value (net assets per the previous year's balance sheet, i.e. largely book values), 25% of the dividend is taxable capital income up to EUR 150,000 per shareholder a year (30% tax = 7.5% effective) and 85% above that (25.5%-28.9%); dividends beyond the 8% return are 75% taxable earned income at progressive rates. The 0.1546 used here is the tax as a share of the gross dividend when two parent shareholders each net EUR 200,000 (EUR 400,000 in total, which is what the projection needs after tax). Per shareholder with gross dividend G above EUR 150,000: taxable capital income = 25% x 150,000 + 85% x (G - 150,000); tax = 30% x 30,000 + 34% x (taxable - 30,000). Net 200,000 needs G = EUR 236,568 and tax EUR 36,568 (15.46% of G); EUR 473,136 gross in total, tax EUR 73,136. (The earlier 0.13 was the tax on a EUR 400,000 gross payout, EUR 52,000, which leaves only EUR 348,000 net.) Bands are the 2026 figures; no statutory indexation was found, so in real terms the rate would rise over time, but the model keeps it fixed. With adult children as shareholders more falls into the 25% band; the 8% limit needs net assets of at least EUR 1.9m per EUR 150,000 of dividend at book values. The company withholds 7.5% / 28%. Repayment of capital from the invested unrestricted equity fund (SVOP) is treated as a dividend for an unlisted company, not a tax-free return.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: No CFC issue for a Finnish company. Passive investment companies are common and accepted, but the general anti-avoidance rule (Act on Assessment Procedure § 28) applies to artificial arrangements, and hidden profit distributions (private use of company assets, under-priced loans) are taxed as dividends or earned income. The Oy must keep double-entry accounts and file an annual return; audit is required above small-company thresholds (not verified for a passive company). Since 2020 a non-business holding company's income falls into the 'other activity' income source, whose losses cannot offset business income.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Finland has no exit tax for individuals (Finnish nationals remain resident for three years after leaving unless they show no essential ties). Liquidation proceeds are taxed for the shareholder as a capital gain at 30%/34% on the excess over the share acquisition cost. After emigration, dividends from the Oy bear Finnish withholding tax (reduced by treaty). The Oy shares are part of the estate for inheritance tax at their fair value; generational business relief does not extend to investment companies.

capital_gains.summary: Gains realised by the Oy on portfolio shares (listed, Finnish or foreign, stakes below 10%) are ordinary taxable income at the 20% corporate rate (2026). The participation exemption only covers fixed-asset shareholdings of at least 10% held for one year. Real estate gains are taxed at 20%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No exemption for portfolio gains. Participation exemption: at least 10% held for one year, shares among the seller's fixed assets in business income, target not a real-estate company, target Finnish/EU/treaty-resident.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Government proposal HE 151/2026 would cut the corporate rate to 18% from tax year 2027; not confirmed as enacted. Transferring an existing personal portfolio into the Oy is a taxable sale at market value for the individual (34%), and Finland gives no step-up on immigration, so the structure works best for cash or assets with small latent gains.

capital_gains.professional_trader: Not relevant at company level: all gains are taxable at 20% either way.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide company taxation; foreign tax credited.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by an unlisted Oy from a listed company in which it holds less than 10% are 100% taxable at 20%. Dividends from companies outside the EU/EEA are also fully taxable. Foreign withholding tax is credited against the Finnish corporate tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Dividends from unlisted companies and from 10%+ holdings are broadly exempt; not relevant for a listed portfolio.

dividends.rate_basis: 100% taxable x 20% CIT = 20% (PwC). Compared with 28.9% (85% x 34%) for a private investor.
dividends.holding_company_notes: This regime models the investment Oy itself.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the permanent home or habitual abode is in Finland, or if present for a continuous period of more than 6 months (temporary absences do not interrupt). Finnish nationals stay resident for 3 full calendar years after leaving unless they prove no essential ties. Foreign nationals cease residence on departure.

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.requirements: Register the right of residence after 3 months; sufficient means for non-workers. Not verified against Migri (site blocked automated access).

routes.name: Residence permit (work, entrepreneur, family)
routes.requirements: No investor or golden visa. Non-EU nationals need a residence permit on another basis (employment, self-employment/entrepreneur, start-up permit with a positive Business Finland statement, family ties). Not verified in detail.

corporate.summary: CIT 20% in 2026. Government proposal HE 151/2026 would cut it to 18% from tax year 2027 and extend loss carry-forward from 10 to 25 years; not yet confirmed as enacted. Pillar Two QDMTT from 2024. Dividends between companies are broadly exempt (participation rules).

income.name: Finland

income_tax.summary: State progressive scale (12.64% to 37.5% as PwC lists it) plus municipal tax of 4.70-10.90% (7.5% used). Employee contributions about 10.17%; YEL for self-employed 24.4%.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: YEL pension 24.4% of confirmed income in 2026 (Ilmarinen), with a 22% discount on the contribution for new entrepreneurs (YEL insurance in force under four years); minimum confirmed income EUR 9,423.09. Self-employed also pay Kela health contributions, which were not found on a page opened. Employee (PwC 2026): pension 7.30% + unemployment 0.89% + health 1.98% (1.10% medicare + 0.88% daily allowance, the latter not collected below EUR 17,255 of salary).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Municipal tax ranges 4.70-10.90% on PwC (Wikipedia gives a 2025 average of 9.28% and a 4.7-19.7% range, which conflicts); PwC's 7.5% is described as the average for non-residents and is used as a stand-in because Helsinki's own rate was not confirmed on any page opened. Church tax (1-2.25%) excluded. The brackets add PwC's state-scale rates to 7.5% and apply from the first euro; Finnish earned-income deductions are not modelled.

regimes.name: Key employee regime (avainhenkilö)
regimes.description: Foreign key employees with special knowledge can be taxed at a flat 25% on Finnish-source salary from the primary employment (PwC 2026; the rate was 32% before 2026). Minimum cash salary of EUR 5,800 in every month, not Finnish resident in the previous five calendar years, up to 84 months; apply within 90 days of starting work. Local employment required. Final tax: no deductions against that income.
regimes.duration_note: Up to 84 months for foreign nationals (60 for returning Finns).

succession.name: Finland
succession.summary: Children are guaranteed half of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Finland has no trust law; foundations exist but family-benefit foundations get no tax exemption and their precise limits were not confirmed.
succession.reserved_share: Direct descendants (and their descendants): half of what they would inherit on intestacy (Code of Inheritance 40/1965, legal share, claim within six months of notice of the will). The surviving spouse may keep the common home and household effects.
succession.foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
succession.trust_note: Finland is not a party to the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention (not in the HCCH table); a foreign trust needs case-by-case analysis. Foundations are governed by the Foundations Act 487/2015; Philea says private-purpose foundations may exist but only public-benefit ones are tax-exempt.
open_questions: Whether new foundations may be set up for family benefit under Act 487/2015 was not confirmed from the statute.
Tax treatment of foreign trusts held by Finnish residents was not sourced.

assumptions: Top rates apply: 34% on capital income (the family's income is far above EUR 30,000) and 85% of listed dividends taxable. No allowances are modelled.

The Oy is funded with a portfolio that has no latent gain (cash, or assets at cost). It distributes dividends within the 8% return on net assets, and the two parents are the only shareholders (the EUR 150,000 band is per shareholder).
Corporate tax is 20% (2026). The proposed cut to 18% from 2027 (HE 151/2026) was still before Parliament's finance committee in September 2026 and is not law.
Foreign dividends come from EU, EEA or treaty-country companies, so the 85% rule and the foreign tax credit apply.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: moving an existing personal portfolio into the Oy is a sale at market value for the individual, taxed as capital income at 30%/34% on the gain, and Finland gives no step-up on immigration (Income Tax Act, capital income; Vero, Selling shares). The engine has no asset-transfer event, so the Oy path assumes a portfolio with no latent gain; for a portfolio with large latent gains the path is overstated.

Needs an engine change: the EUR 150,000 band, the EUR 30,000 capital-income threshold and the 8% limit are fixed nominal amounts, so the Oy's payout tax rate rises in real terms over 60 years; the engine holds the payout rate constant.

Whether the Tax Administration applies a discount for deferred tax to the market value of the Oy's shares for inheritance tax (guide 'Yritysvarallisuuden arvostaminen perintö- ja lahjaverotuksessa', Finnish only) was not read; the check uses full portfolio value.
The Oy's annual running cost (bookkeeping, audit) is not in the tax file; the Oy check carries none.

Private family foundations were considered and not added: sources disagree whether Finnish foundations may serve private (family) purposes, permission from the Patent and Registration Office is needed (Foundations Act 487/2015), and none of the sources shows their use for a family portfolio. Finland has no trust law.

The Foundations, Double Taxation and Income Tax Acts and the Vero 'Relief for international double taxation' guidance were read only through search results or not at all; no statute section is cited for that reason. Vero's page on dividends of an unlisted company receiving listed dividends was seen only as a search excerpt.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Gains are capital income at 34% above EUR 30,000; dividends from listed companies are 85% taxable at 34% (28.9%), with credit for foreign withholding; no wealth tax. Inheritance tax per child runs from 7% to 19%, 19% above EUR 1,000,000. Finland has no special regime for wealthy arrivals: the key-employee regime needs Finnish employment.

paths.name: Private investment company (Oy)
paths.note: A Finnish Oy owned by the parents pays 20% on portfolio dividends (fully taxable below 10%) and on gains. Dividends to the parents from an unlisted company are taxed lightly: 25% of the first EUR 150,000 per shareholder within an 8% return is taxable capital income. The shares are in the estate at market value; generational business relief does not cover an investment company.
